title: Pullback on cohomology over objects along a morphism of sites
statement: Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites given by the continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with $f_*=u^s$, $f^{-1}$ its left adjoint on abelian sheaves, which is exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact] and unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to f_*f^{-1}$. For $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathcal A\in\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ choose an injective resolution $\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and an injective resolution $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal J^\bullet$; as $f^{-1}$ is exact, $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution, so there is a map of complexes $\beta:f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ under $f^{-1}\mathcal A$, unique up to homotopy. Define $f^*:H^p(V,\mathcal A)\to H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal A)$ as $H^p$ of $\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta}\Gamma(V,f_*f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)=\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta}\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet)$. Then: (1) $f^*$ does not depend on the choices, and in degree $0$ it is $\eta_{\mathcal A}(V):\mathcal A(V)\to(f^{-1}\mathcal A)(u(V))$; (2) $f^*$ is natural in $\mathcal A$: $H^p(f^{-1}\varphi)\circ f^*=f^*\circ H^p(\varphi)$ for $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$; (3) for a short exact sequence $S:0\to\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A''\to0$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, with image $f^{-1}S:0\to f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal A'\to f^{-1}\mathcal A''\to0$, a short exact sequence of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], let $\delta^p_{V,S}:H^p(V,\mathcal A'')\to H^{p+1}(V,\mathcal A)$ and $\delta^p_{u(V),f^{-1}S}:H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal A'')\to H^{p+1}(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal A)$ be the connecting maps of the long exact sequences of $H^\bullet(V,-)=R^\bullet\Gamma(V,-)$ and $H^\bullet(u(V),-)=R^\bullet\Gamma(u(V),-)$ computed from horseshoe resolutions, which do not depend on the horseshoe resolution and make these functors $\delta$-functors [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (these are the connecting maps of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact]); then $f^*\circ\delta^p_{V,S}=\delta^p_{u(V),f^{-1}S}\circ f^*$ for all $p\ge0$; equivalently, with (2), $(f^*)_p$ is a morphism of $\delta$-functors [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] from $(H^p(V,-),\delta_{V,-})_p$ to $(H^p(u(V),f^{-1}(-)),\delta_{u(V),f^{-1}(-)})_p$, and it is the unique one which is $\eta(V)$ in degree $0$, $(H^p(V,-),\delta_{V,-})_p$ being universal (the connecting maps obtained from distinguished triangles in [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] are not addressed here); (4) for a second morphism of sites $g:\mathcal E\to\mathcal D$ given by $v:\mathcal D\to\mathcal E$, so that $f\circ g$ is given by $v\circ u$, one has $(f\circ g)^*=H^p(c)\circ g^*\circ f^*$ on $H^p(V,\mathcal A)$, where $c:g^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal A$ is the canonical isomorphism of left adjoints of $(f\circ g)_*=f_*g_*$ (compatible with the units) [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition].

proof.text: *Setting.* $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ are abelian with enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives], so every abelian sheaf has an injective resolution $s:\mathcal F\to P^\bullet$ with $P^q=0$ for $q<0$ [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (1). $\Gamma(W,-)$ is left exact additive and $H^p(W,-)=R^p\Gamma(W,-)$ for $W\in\{V,u(V)\}$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2); by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] $R^p\Gamma(W,-)$ is a functor and for each such resolution there is an isomorphism $\iota^p_P:H^p(W,\mathcal F)\to H^p(\Gamma(W,P^\bullet))$ with $H^p(W,h)=(\iota^p_Q)^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(W,\varphi))\iota^p_P$ for every morphism $h:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, resolution $t:\mathcal G\to Q^\bullet$ and morphism of complexes $\varphi$ with $\varphi^0s=th$. The functor $f^{-1}$ is additive and exact [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]. Since $f_*=u^s$ is precomposition with $u$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (3), $\Gamma(V,f_*\mathcal G)=\mathcal G(u(V))=\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal G)$ and $\Gamma(V,f_*\psi)=\Gamma(u(V),\psi)$ for $\psi$ in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$. The unit $\eta$ is natural: $f_*f^{-1}(\varphi)\circ\eta_{\mathcal F}=\eta_{\mathcal F'}\circ\varphi$ for $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$; on sections over $V$ this reads $\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}\varphi)\circ\eta_{\mathcal F}(V)=\eta_{\mathcal F'}(V)\circ\Gamma(V,\varphi)$. Applied to the differentials of a complex $K^\bullet$ of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$, it shows that $\eta_{K}:\Gamma(V,K^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}K^\bullet)$, $a\mapsto\eta_{K^n}(V)(a)$ in degree $n$, is a morphism of complexes, natural in $K^\bullet$.

proof.text: *Lifting principle.* Let $\mathcal X$ be $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ or $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$. (a) Let $t:X\to P^\bullet$ be a resolution, i.e. $P^q=0$ for $q<0$ and $0\to X\xrightarrow{t}P^0\to P^1\to\cdots$ exact, equivalently $t:X[0]\to P^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism ($P^\bullet$ need not consist of injectives); let $r:Y\to Q^\bullet$ be an injective resolution with $Q^q=0$ for $q<0$, and $h:X\to Y$. Then there is a morphism of complexes $\varphi:P^\bullet\to Q^\bullet$ with $\varphi^0t=rh$, and any two such are homotopic. Indeed $Q^\bullet$ is bounded below with injective terms, hence K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] (2), so the localization induces bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal X)}(N,Q^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal X)}(N,Q^\bullet)$ for every complex $N$ [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; these carry $-\circ t$ to $-\circ Q(t)$, which is bijective because the quasi-isomorphism $t$ becomes invertible in $D(\mathcal X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. So $-\circ t:\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(P^\bullet,Q^\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}_K(X[0],Q^\bullet)$ is bijective: there is $\varphi$ with $\varphi t\simeq rh$, unique up to homotopy. A homotopy between two morphisms $X[0]\to Q^\bullet$ consists of maps $X[0]^n\to Q^{n-1}$, which are all $0$ ($X[0]^n=0$ for $n\ne0$, $Q^{-1}=0$); so $\varphi t\simeq rh$ means $\varphi^0t=rh$. (b) An additive functor ($\Gamma(W,-)$, $f^{-1}$) carries a homotopy $k$ between morphisms of complexes to a homotopy (apply it to $\varphi-\varphi'=dk+kd$), so homotopic morphisms $\varphi\simeq\varphi'$ give $H^p(\Gamma(W,\varphi))=H^p(\Gamma(W,\varphi'))$. (c) If $t:X\to P^\bullet$ is a resolution and $\psi:P^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ a quasi-isomorphism to a complex of injectives with $J^q=0$ for $q<0$, then $\psi^0t:X\to J^\bullet$ is an injective resolution (the composite $X[0]\to P^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism).

proof.text: *The construction is well posed.* Let $s:\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $r:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ be injective resolutions zero in negative degrees. As $f^{-1}$ is exact and additive [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $0\to f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal I^0\to f^{-1}\mathcal I^1\to\cdots$ is exact, i.e. $f^{-1}(s):f^{-1}\mathcal A\to f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ is a resolution, so step 2(a) (with $h=\mathrm{id}$) gives $\beta:f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ with $\beta^0\circ f^{-1}(s)=r$, unique up to homotopy. Put $c_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}:=\Gamma(u(V),\beta)\circ\eta_{\mathcal I}:\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet)$, a morphism of complexes (step 1), and $f^*_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}:=(\iota^p_{\mathcal J})^{-1}\circ H^p(c)\circ\iota^p_{\mathcal I}:H^p(V,\mathcal A)\to H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\mathcal A)$: this is the map of the statement (read through the isomorphisms $\iota$ of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] which identify $H^p(\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J^\bullet))$ with the derived functors). If $\beta'\simeq\beta$ then $c_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta')}\simeq c_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}$ by step 2(b) applied to $\Gamma(u(V),-)$, so $f^*_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}$ depends only on $(s,r)$.

proof.text: *Naturality for arbitrary choices.* Let $\varphi:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$, and let $(s,r,\beta)$ and $(s',r',\beta')$ be choices as in step 3 for $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A'$, with complexes $\mathcal I,\mathcal J$ and $\mathcal I',\mathcal J'$ and chain maps $c,c'$. Claim: $f^*_{(\mathcal I',\mathcal J',\beta')}\circ H^p(V,\varphi)=H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\varphi)\circ f^*_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}$. By step 2(a) choose $\tilde\varphi:\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal I'^\bullet$ with $\tilde\varphi^0s=s'\varphi$ and $\psi:\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$ with $\psi^0r=r'\circ f^{-1}\varphi$. The morphisms $\psi\beta$ and $\beta'\circ f^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)$ from $f^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet$ to $\mathcal J'^\bullet$ satisfy $\psi^0\beta^0f^{-1}(s)=\psi^0r=r'f^{-1}(\varphi)$ and $\beta'^0f^{-1}(\tilde\varphi^0)f^{-1}(s)=\beta'^0f^{-1}(s')f^{-1}(\varphi)=r'f^{-1}(\varphi)$ ($f^{-1}$ is a functor), so by the uniqueness in step 2(a) (for the resolution $f^{-1}(s)$, step 3) $\psi\beta\simeq\beta'f^{-1}(\tilde\varphi)$. Naturality of $\eta$ (step 1) gives $\eta_{\mathcal I'}\circ\Gamma(V,\tilde\varphi)=\Gamma(u(V),f^{-1}\tilde\varphi)\circ\eta_{\mathcal I}$. Hence $c'\circ\Gamma(V,\tilde\varphi)=\Gamma(u(V),\beta'f^{-1}\tilde\varphi)\circ\eta_{\mathcal I}\simeq\Gamma(u(V),\psi\beta)\circ\eta_{\mathcal I}=\Gamma(u(V),\psi)\circ c$, and by step 2(b) $H^p(c')H^p(\Gamma(V,\tilde\varphi))=H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\psi))H^p(c)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift], $H^p(V,\varphi)=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I'})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(V,\tilde\varphi))\iota^p_{\mathcal I}$ and $H^p(u(V),f^{-1}\varphi)=(\iota^p_{\mathcal J'})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(u(V),\psi))\iota^p_{\mathcal J}$; conjugating the last equality by the $\iota$'s gives the claim.

proof.text: *Clauses (1) and (2).* Independence: apply step 4 with $\mathcal A'=\mathcal A$ and $\varphi=\mathrm{id}$; since $H^p(V,-)$ and $H^p(u(V),-)$ are functors [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] and $f^{-1}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $f^*_{(\mathcal I',\mathcal J',\beta')}=f^*_{(\mathcal I,\mathcal J,\beta)}$ for any two choices; write $f^*$. Then step 4 is clause (2). Degree $0$: the identification $H^0(W,\mathcal F)=\mathcal F(W)$ of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] is $\epsilon_{\mathcal F}=(\iota^0_P)^{-1}e_P$, where $e_P:\mathcal F(W)\to H^0(\Gamma(W,P^\bullet))=\ker\Gamma(W,d^0)$ is induced by $\Gamma(W,s_P)$ and is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2); it does not depend on $P$, since for a second resolution $P'$ and $\varphi$ with $\varphi^0s_P=s_{P'}$ one has $H^0(\Gamma(W,\varphi))e_P=e_{P'}$ and $(\iota^0_{P'})^{-1}H^0(\Gamma(W,\varphi))\iota^0_P=\mathrm{id}$. For $x\in\mathcal A(V)$: $c(s(x))=\beta^0(\eta_{\mathcal I^0}(V)(s(x)))=\beta^0\bigl(f^{-1}(s)(\eta_{\mathcal A}(V)(x))\bigr)=r(\eta_{\mathcal A}(V)(x))$ (naturality of $\eta$ at $s$, then $\beta^0f^{-1}(s)=r$), sections over $u(V)$. So $H^0(c)e_{\mathcal I}=e_{\mathcal J}\circ\eta_{\mathcal A}(V)$, i.e. $f^*\circ\epsilon_{\mathcal A}=\epsilon_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}\circ\eta_{\mathcal A}(V)$: in degree $0$, $f^*$ is $\eta_{\mathcal A}(V):\mathcal A(V)\to(f^{-1}\mathcal A)(u(V))$.

proof.text: *Clause (4) (composition).* Write $\eta^f,\eta^g,\eta^{fg}$ for the units of $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$, $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, $(f\circ g)^{-1}\dashv(f\circ g)_*$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition] (2), (3) (applied with its $u,v$ equal to our $v,u$): $(f\circ g)_*=(v\circ u)^s=u^sv^s=f_*g_*$, and the isomorphism $c:g^{-1}f^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(f\circ g)^{-1}$ satisfies $(f\circ g)_*(c_{\mathcal F})\circ f_*(\eta^g_{f^{-1}\mathcal F})\circ\eta^f_{\mathcal F}=\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal F}$; on sections over $V$ (step 1, $\Gamma(V,f_*g_*-)=\Gamma(v(u(V)),-)$): $\eta^g_{f^{-1}\mathcal F}(u(V))\circ\eta^f_{\mathcal F}(V)=\Gamma(vu(V),c_{\mathcal F}^{-1})\circ\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal F}(V)$. Choose $s:\mathcal A\to\mathcal I^\bullet$, $r:f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal J^\bullet$, $\beta$ as in step 3 for $f$, and for $g$ and the sheaf $f^{-1}\mathcal A$ with its resolution $r$: an injective resolution $r_E:g^{-1}f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal L^\bullet$ and $\gamma:g^{-1}\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal L^\bullet$ with $\gamma^0g^{-1}(r)=r_E$. By step 3 and clause (1), $g^*f^*=(\iota^p_{(\mathcal L,r_E)})^{-1}H^p\bigl(\Gamma(vu(V),\gamma)\eta^g_{\mathcal J}\Gamma(u(V),\beta)\eta^f_{\mathcal I}\bigr)\iota^p_{\mathcal I}$. Naturality of $\eta^g$ at $\beta$ gives $\eta^g_{\mathcal J}\Gamma(u(V),\beta)=\Gamma(vu(V),g^{-1}\beta)\eta^g_{f^{-1}\mathcal I}$, and with the displayed identity the chain map is $\Gamma(vu(V),\beta'')\circ\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal I}$, $\beta'':=\gamma\circ g^{-1}(\beta)\circ c_{\mathcal I}^{-1}:(f\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal L^\bullet$. Put $\rho:=r_E\circ c_{\mathcal A}^{-1}:(f\circ g)^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal L^0$, an injective resolution ($c_{\mathcal A}$ is an isomorphism). By naturality of $c$, $\beta''^0(f\circ g)^{-1}(s)=\gamma^0g^{-1}(\beta^0)g^{-1}f^{-1}(s)c_{\mathcal A}^{-1}=\gamma^0g^{-1}(r)c_{\mathcal A}^{-1}=\rho$, so $(s,(\mathcal L,\rho),\beta'')$ is a choice for $(f\circ g)^*$ (step 3, clause (1)) and $(f\circ g)^*=(\iota^p_{(\mathcal L,\rho)})^{-1}H^p(\Gamma(vu(V),\beta'')\eta^{fg}_{\mathcal I})\iota^p_{\mathcal I}$. Finally $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal L}$ lifts $c_{\mathcal A}$ ($\mathrm{id}\circ r_E=\rho\circ c_{\mathcal A}$), so $H^p(vu(V),c_{\mathcal A})=(\iota^p_{(\mathcal L,\rho)})^{-1}\iota^p_{(\mathcal L,r_E)}$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. Therefore $(f\circ g)^*=H^p(c_{\mathcal A})\circ g^*\circ f^*$.

proof.text: *Compatible horseshoe resolutions on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$.* Let $S:0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal A'\xrightarrow{a'}\mathcal A''\to0$ be short exact in $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$; write $\mathcal A_1,\mathcal A_2,\mathcal A_3$ for $\mathcal A,\mathcal A',\mathcal A''$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses] choose injective resolutions $s_k:\mathcal A_k\to\mathcal I_k^\bullet$ zero in negative degrees and morphisms of complexes $i:\mathcal I_1\to\mathcal I_2$, $q:\mathcal I_2\to\mathcal I_3$ with $i^0s_1=s_2a$, $q^0s_2=s_3a'$ and $0\to\mathcal I_1^n\to\mathcal I_2^n\to\mathcal I_3^n\to0$ short exact: a horseshoe resolution of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor]. Since $f^{-1}$ is exact and additive [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact], $0\to f^{-1}\mathcal I_1^\bullet\to f^{-1}\mathcal I_2^\bullet\to f^{-1}\mathcal I_3^\bullet\to0$ is a sequence of complexes of $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$, zero in negative degrees, short exact in each degree, and $f^{-1}(s_k)$ are resolutions (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses-complexes] there are complexes of injectives $\mathcal J_k^\bullet$ zero in negative degrees, morphisms $j:\mathcal J_1\to\mathcal J_2$, $q':\mathcal J_2\to\mathcal J_3$ with $0\to\mathcal J_1^n\to\mathcal J_2^n\to\mathcal J_3^n\to0$ short exact, and quasi-isomorphisms $\beta_k:f^{-1}\mathcal I_k^\bullet\to\mathcal J_k^\bullet$ with $\beta_2f^{-1}(i)=j\beta_1$, $\beta_3f^{-1}(q)=q'\beta_2$. By step 2(c), $r_k:=\beta_k^0f^{-1}(s_k)$ is an injective resolution of $f^{-1}\mathcal A_k$; moreover $j^0r_1=\beta_2^0f^{-1}(i^0s_1)=\beta_2^0f^{-1}(s_2)f^{-1}(a)=r_2f^{-1}(a)$ and likewise $q'^0r_2=r_3f^{-1}(a')$. So $(r_k,j,q')$ is a horseshoe resolution of $f^{-1}S$, and $(s_k,r_k,\beta_k)$ is an admissible choice computing $f^*$ on $\mathcal A_k$ (step 3, clause (1)).

proof.text: *Clause (3) (connecting maps).* With the data of step 7 put $c_k:=\Gamma(u(V),\beta_k)\circ\eta_{\mathcal I_k}:\Gamma(V,\mathcal I_k^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J_k^\bullet)$. These form a morphism of sequences of complexes: by naturality of $\eta$ at $i$ (step 1), $c_2\Gamma(V,i)=\Gamma(u(V),\beta_2f^{-1}(i))\eta_{\mathcal I_1}=\Gamma(u(V),j\beta_1)\eta_{\mathcal I_1}=\Gamma(u(V),j)c_1$, and likewise $c_3\Gamma(V,q)=\Gamma(u(V),q')c_2$. The rows $0\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal I_1^\bullet)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal I_2^\bullet)\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal I_3^\bullet)\to0$ and $0\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J_1^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J_2^\bullet)\to\Gamma(u(V),\mathcal J_3^\bullet)\to0$ are short exact in each degree (as stated in [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor]: the degreewise sequences split because $\mathcal I_1^n$, $\mathcal J_1^n$ are injective, and the additive $\Gamma(W,-)$ preserves the splitting identities). Let $\partial_{\mathcal C}$, $\partial_{\mathcal D}$ be their connecting morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality], $H^{p+1}(c_1)\circ\partial^p_{\mathcal C}=\partial^p_{\mathcal D}\circ H^p(c_3)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (1), computing the connecting maps from these horseshoe resolutions, $\delta^p_{V,S}=(\iota^{p+1}_{\mathcal I_1})^{-1}\partial^p_{\mathcal C}\iota^p_{\mathcal I_3}$ and $\delta^p_{u(V),f^{-1}S}=(\iota^{p+1}_{\mathcal J_1})^{-1}\partial^p_{\mathcal D}\iota^p_{\mathcal J_3}$, and by step 3 $f^*=(\iota_{\mathcal J_k})^{-1}H(c_k)\iota_{\mathcal I_k}$ on $\mathcal A_k$. Hence $f^*\delta^p_{V,S}=(\iota^{p+1}_{\mathcal J_1})^{-1}H^{p+1}(c_1)\partial^p_{\mathcal C}\iota^p_{\mathcal I_3}=(\iota^{p+1}_{\mathcal J_1})^{-1}\partial^p_{\mathcal D}H^p(c_3)\iota^p_{\mathcal I_3}=\delta^p_{u(V),f^{-1}S}f^*$.

proof.text: *The $\delta$-functor formulation.* By [lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor] (2), applied to the left exact additive $\Gamma(V,-)$ on $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ and $\Gamma(u(V),-)$ on $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ (step 1), $(H^p(V,-),\delta_{V,-})_p$ and $(H^p(u(V),-),\delta_{u(V),-})_p$ are $\delta$-functors [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor]. Put $G^p:=H^p(u(V),f^{-1}(-))$ and $\delta_{G,S}:=\delta_{u(V),f^{-1}S}$. Then $(G^p,\delta_G)$ is a $\delta$-functor on $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$: $G^p$ is additive as a composite of additive functors ($f^{-1}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact]); $f^{-1}S$ is short exact (same node), so the long sequence of $G$ for $S$ is the exact sequence of $f^{-1}S$; a morphism $(x,y,z)$ of short exact sequences $S\to S'$ gives the morphism $(f^{-1}x,f^{-1}y,f^{-1}z):f^{-1}S\to f^{-1}S'$, so naturality of $\delta_G$ is naturality of $\delta_{u(V),-}$. By clause (2) the $(f^*)_p$ are natural transformations $H^p(V,-)\to G^p$ and by clause (3) they commute with the connecting maps: $f^*$ is a morphism of $\delta$-functors. Universality: for $n>0$ and $\mathcal A$ choose a monomorphism $\mathcal A\to\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I$ injective [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaves-enough-injectives]; $H^n(V,\mathcal I)=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-injective-vanishing], so $H^n(V,\mathcal A)\to H^n(V,\mathcal I)$ is zero and $(H^p(V,-),\delta_{V,-})$ is universal [lem-weil-pbc-effaceable-delta-functor-universal]. Hence $f^*$ is the unique morphism of $\delta$-functors whose degree-$0$ component is $f^*_0$, which is $\eta(V)$ under $H^0=\Gamma$ (step 5).

split_report.summary: Proof written in nine steps from Stacks Cohomology 01F7/01F8/01FB (ringed spaces; sites via 08J6) and Derived 013P/013S/013T: setting (enough injectives, iota isomorphisms of map-via-lift, f_* = u^s, naturality of the unit); lifting principle through a non-injective resolution into a bounded below injective complex (K-injective leaves; homotopies X[0] -> Q vanish); the construction is well posed; naturality for arbitrary choices, which gives independence (1) and naturality (2); degree 0 = eta(V); composition (4) from the unit compatibility of lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition (3); compatible horseshoes on C and D (013T for complexes applied to f^{-1} of a horseshoe on C); delta-compatibility (3) by naturality of the connecting map of a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes; and the delta-functor/universality formulation. Clause (3) of the statement made precise: the delta is the horseshoe delta (the one of lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact), made well defined and natural by the new node lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor; the triangle delta of lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor is explicitly not addressed. 'f^{-1} exact on abelian sheaves', asserted in the statement, now cites the new node lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact (Stacks 04JC). New nodes: lem-weil-pbc-site-pullback-abelian-exact, lem-weil-pbc-horseshoe-delta-functor, lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-ses-complexes (Stacks 013T for complexes, part (2)); all unsplit, no Mathlib match.
